files.purpose: This is the Xcode 26 'Icon Composer' project file for Droppy Code's app icon (ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME: AppIcon in project.yml, line 47), compiled at build time into the .icns/asset-catalog app icon rather than loaded by any Swift code at runtime (no 'AppIcon' reference exists anywhere under DroppyCode/**/*.swift). It declares a layered, appearance- and platform-specialized icon: a background tile with separate light and dark linear-gradient fill specializations, four image layers (two mascot renditions plus two matching shadow renditions, each with glass/opacity/position specializations for light, dark and tinted appearance) plus an SVG overlay layer, a group-level shadow and translucency setting, and supported-platforms metadata restricting circular (watchOS) rendering while sharing the square variant.
key_symbols: groups[0].layers (mascot dark, shadow dark, mascot , shadow def, SVG Image)
platform_assumptions: Entirely an Apple Icon Composer / Xcode asset-catalog artifact (macOS 26 'Liquid Glass' adaptive icon pipeline): 'glass-specializations', 'translucency' and per-appearance (light/dark/tinted) layer opacity have no Windows equivalent icon format.
Color stops mix 'srgb:' and 'display-p3:' color-space-tagged literals, a wide-gamut display convention that does not apply to the Windows .ico/.png icon pipeline.
'supported-platforms.circles: ["watchOS"]' shows this same icon.json is shared with a watchOS circular-icon target that has no Windows counterpart at all.
ui_elements: Droppy Code's own app icon (Dock/Finder/Launchpad/.icns), not an in-app control; never rendered by app UI code, only referenced by the Xcode build settings
feature_notes: B2->B3 changed exactly 4 lines (lines 6-7 in B3): the light-appearance background linear-gradient stops moved from a sky-blue pair ('display-p3:0.56863,0.76863,1.00000,1.00000' -> 'srgb:0.14510,0.50196,1.00000,1.00000') to a purple/indigo pair ('srgb:0.51765,0.52549,0.96471,1.00000' -> 'srgb:0.07059,0.09804,0.92941,1.00000'); confirmed via `git diff 1fbf81e61e28a079508a074c01ee1830a9cc23dc HEAD -- DroppyCode/Resources/AppIcon.icon/icon.json`, which shows only this one hunk.

The dark-appearance fill-specialization (display-p3 grays, lines 12-19), both mascot/shadow image layers, all glass/opacity/position specializations, the group shadow, translucency, and supported-platforms block are byte-identical to B2 — this is a pure brand-color refresh of Droppy Code's own light-mode icon background, nothing structural.

OWNER DECISION OD-0015 ('App icon: the Marrow icon the owner already finalized') already rules that the Windows port does not derive its icon from this file at all: the port ships the owner's own pre-finalized Marrow icon (src/Marrow.App/Assets/icon.svg, icon-small.svg, icon-mono.svg, icon.ico, icon.png — three arcs around a white core on a dark navy tile, explicitly commented 'Original artwork for this project; not derived from Droppy or Droppy Code artwork'), and this supersedes source parity for the whole AppIcon.icon bundle. Verified by reading src/Marrow.App/Assets/icon.svg (dark navy/near-black tile gradient #1D2147/#121529/#0A0C18 with blue/purple/teal arm gradients, none of which resemble either the B2 or B3 icon.json background colors) and by porting/owner_decisions.md lines 245-256.

No requirement or UI-contract record cites this file: grep -n "AppIcon" and grep -n "icon\.json" (case-insensitive) return zero matches across every file in porting/spec/*.json, porting/ui_contract.json and porting/parity_matrix.json.
